decisions.description: Withdrawals are capped at a daily limit of 5000.00 per account, rejected with 'daily-limit' when exceeded.
The daily withdrawal counter is never reset, so the 'daily' limit is effectively a lifetime limit for the ledger instance.
The daily limit counts only the withdrawn amount, not the fee.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00.
The 1% fee is rounded up to the next cent (ceiling), a rounding mode the plan does not specify.
Cent rounding adds a 1e-7 epsilon before rounding to compensate for floating-point error, which can shift values just below a half upward.
The fee is charged on top of the withdrawal amount (debited in addition) rather than deducted from it.
Withdrawals, transfers and split payments are rejected with 'insufficient-funds' if they would make the balance negative; overdraft policy is not in the plan.
For withdrawals the funds check includes the fee, so a withdrawal is rejected if the balance covers the amount but not amount plus fee.
When a withdrawal fails both the funds and daily-limit checks, insufficient-funds is reported first.
A repeated transaction id returns success without re-applying and without checking that the retry has the same account, amount or operation.
Transaction ids share one global namespace across all accounts and all operation types.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with an invalid amount (or empty recipients) is rejected even if the id was already accepted.
Rejected operations do not record their transaction id, so a retry of a rejected id can later succeed.
Accounts are created implicitly on first use by any operation, including withdrawal, transfer source and split recipients; there is no unknown-account error.
Accounts are opened even when the operation is subsequently rejected (e.g. insufficient funds).
Querying the balance of an unknown account returns 0 and its history returns an empty list instead of an error.
The positivity check is applied to the raw amount, so amounts that round to 0 cents (e.g. 0.004) are accepted and recorded as zero entries, and a zero-cent withdrawal still incurs the 0.50 fee.
Infinity passes the amount > 0 check and is accepted as a valid amount.
Foreign deposits reject a non-positive exchange rate, reported with the generic reason 'invalid-amount'.
Foreign deposits whose converted value rounds to 0 cents are rejected with 'amount-too-small'.
Foreign conversion is rounded half away from zero (via toCents) instead of half to even.
Foreign deposits are recorded as a plain 'deposit' entry with no currency, original amount or rate kept.
Transfers and split payments are charged no fee; only withdrawals are.
In a split, leftover cents from uneven division go one each to the first recipients in list order.
A split with an empty recipient list is rejected with 'no-recipients'.
Split recipients may repeat or include the payer, and recipients whose share is 0 cents still get a zero entry.
A split records a single 'split-out' debit for the whole amount on the payer rather than one entry per recipient.
Interest is rounded down (floored) to the cent, with a 1e-7 epsilon.
The interest rate is interpreted as a percentage (5 means 5%), and simple (non-compounding) interest is used.
Zero or negative interest rates and non-positive day counts are rejected; fractional days are accepted.
Interest that rounds to 0 cents returns success without recording an entry or the transaction id.
Errors are returned as {ok:false, reason} values with fixed reason strings rather than thrown.
History entries store amounts as unsigned decimal units (not cents), with direction implied only by kind.
Balances are exposed as decimal units converted from cents.
